description: A small tree 3-7 m tall on the Lofoten coast, with smooth silvery-grey bark and feathery leaves of eleven to fifteen toothed leaflets, scattered through the birch woods and on rocky slopes. Flat white flower heads in early summer become heavy bunches of scarlet berries that thrushes and waxwings strip in autumn, when the leaves turn orange and red.

season_notes.winter: Bare grey twigs with fat, hairy, purplish buds; a few berries left for waxwings.
season_notes.spring: Bare until late May, then the downy new leaves unfold.
season_notes.summer: Creamy-white, strong-smelling flower heads in June and July; green berries reddening by August.
season_notes.fall: Scarlet berries and orange-red leaves in September; fieldfares and redwings arrive to eat them.

notes: Grown from Oregon ash: no Rosaceae tree with pinnate leaves in the library (toyon and the mountain mahoganies have simple leaves), so the template is chosen for the leaf type and the small tree architecture rather than the family. COMPROMISES: the rowan's flat corymbs and drooping berry bunches are the generator's round 'cluster'; the leaflets are drawn without their saw-toothed margins. Heights, phenology and colours are the drafter's knowledge (no Norwegian flora source was read): flowering June-July this far north, berries ripe August-September and taken by fieldfare, redwing, waxwing and starling (the starling is in the library; its range model is Californian), browsed hard by red deer and moose so that saplings stay bushy. Lofoten's calendar: polar night in December and early January, birch bare from about October to the end of May, leaf-out in late May and June, autumn yellow in September; the climate is oceanic, winters mild for the latitude, the treeline low (a few hundred metres) under salt wind.
